tip_title: November Is When You Should Know How Your Policy Handles Ice Dams
topic: Winter Storm Home Insurance - Ice Dam Coverage
blurb:
💡 **Insurance Tip: November Is When You Should Know How Your Policy Handles Ice Dams**

Ice dams form when heat escapes through your roof, melts snow near the peak, and then that water refreezes at the cold eaves — building up a ridge of ice that can force water under shingles and into your walls and ceilings. Standard homeowners policies generally cover the resulting interior water damage when it's sudden and accidental, but here's the catch: if your attic insulation is thin or your ventilation has been a known issue for a while, an adjuster may frame it as a maintenance problem rather than a covered loss. The coverage turns on whether the damage looks sudden or whether it looks like deferred upkeep. Before the first hard freeze, it's worth knowing which category your roof situation would fall into.

Have questions about how winter damage claims tend to get evaluated under your specific policy? Your Peachy agent can walk you through what to look for before anything happens.

📖 [Learn more from Insurance.com](https://www.insurance.com/natural-disasters/insurance-for-winter-storms)

tip_title: Your Home Policy Has a Hidden Math Rule That Can Reduce Your Claim Payout
topic: Home Insurance - Dwelling Coverage and the 80% Coinsurance Rule
blurb:
💡 **Insurance Tip: Your Home Policy Has a Hidden Math Rule That Can Reduce Your Claim Payout**

Most homeowners know their policy has a dwelling coverage limit — the number that pays to rebuild the structure if something goes wrong. What most people don't know is that there's a rule baked into most policies that says if your coverage drops below 80% of your home's actual rebuild cost, your insurer can reduce payouts even on partial losses. Not just total losses. Partial ones too. Construction costs have climbed significantly over the last few years, so the number you set three or four years ago may have drifted below that threshold without you ever changing anything on purpose. Pull up your declarations page and see what your dwelling limit is — then ask whether that number still reflects what it would cost to rebuild your home at today's labor and material prices.

Not sure if your dwelling limit is keeping pace? Your Peachy agent can walk through the rebuild cost calculation with you — it's one of the most useful fifteen minutes you can spend on your policy.

📖 [Learn more from MoneyGeek](https://www.moneygeek.com/insurance/homeowners/what-is-dwelling-coverage/)
summary: Covers the 80% coinsurance rule in homeowners policies — specifically that falling below 80% of a home's rebuild cost allows the insurer to reduce claim payouts on partial losses — framed as a check on whether rising construction costs have eroded dwelling coverage adequacy.
